answer: An agent economy can make reputation costly to duplicate by requiring each identity to lock a scarce token as collateral before it can submit work. A verifier releases the stake only after the agent’s claims survive challenge and match an external anchor, such as a signed delivery receipt; proven fraud burns part of it. The zenith of an agent’s reputation then reflects repeated costly success, while a beacon marks verified providers. A sybil attacker must fund every fake identity and risks losing each stake.
